lines.text: Everyone thinks a haunted house is a dark hallway and a guy in a mask. So you rent a barn, buy a fog machine, hire three scare actors, and open on Friday.
Then a guest gets lost in the maze, and at midnight your scare actors find her asleep in a coffin.
So you add a headcount: a clicker at the entrance, a clicker at the exit, and a live board. At closing, in minus out is zero.
Then a scare actor jumps out too early, and the whole queue watches the trick from outside. Nobody screams. One kid waves.
So you add trigger pads. A guest steps on the pad, a two-second delay, a buzz in the actor's earpiece, and then: boo.
Now every scare lands on the right person, and the queue outside only hears screaming.
Then on opening night the fog sets off the smoke alarm, and three fire trucks join the queue.
So you add a haze machine, a map of every detector, and a sign-off with the fire officer before the doors open.
Then a guest panics in room four, and can't find the way out, because the way out is painted to look like a wall.
So you add a safe word. Say it, and a red light comes on, every actor freezes, and a hidden door opens in the wall.
Then Halloween sells out. Two thousand people show up at seven, the queue wraps the parking lot, and the maze jams solid.
So you add timed tickets. Groups of six, every ninety seconds, and the clickers keep score at both doors.
A year later, Hollow Pines is safe, timed, counted, and very, very scary.
Then one Friday, at closing, the clickers don't match.
